value.title: Introduction to Transformers
value.summary: This chapter introduces the transformer architecture as a foundational technology in modern AI, particularly within large language models. It sets the stage for understanding the attention mechanism by highlighting its significance in processing sequential data.

value.title: Origins of Attention Mechanism
value.summary: The chapter traces the attention mechanism back to the seminal 2017 paper 'Attention is All You Need', establishing its role as a core innovation in neural network design for natural language processing.

value.title: Tokenization and Word Embeddings
value.summary: It explains the process of tokenization, where input text is broken into discrete units, and how each token is mapped to a high-dimensional vector (embedding) that encodes semantic meaning in a continuous space.

value.title: Semantic Meaning in Embedding Space
value.summary: This chapter explores how directions in high-dimensional embedding space correspond to semantic concepts such as gender, and how transformers refine word representations by incorporating contextual information.

value.title: Contextual Ambiguity and Attention
value.summary: It addresses the challenge of word ambiguity (e.g., 'mole' in different contexts) and introduces attention as the mechanism that resolves such ambiguities by dynamically adjusting embeddings based on surrounding context.

value.title: Contextual Refinement of Word Vectors
value.summary: The chapter demonstrates how attention updates word embeddings—such as 'tower'—to reflect specific meanings (e.g., Eiffel Tower) based on preceding context, enabling precise semantic representation.

value.title: Information Flow and Attention Blocks
value.summary: It describes how attention blocks allow information to be transferred across distant tokens in a sequence, enabling the final output vector to encode rich, context-dependent meaning for next-token prediction.

value.title: Computational Mechanics of Attention
value.summary: This chapter details the mathematical operations of attention: query and key computation via matrix multiplication, dot product scoring, and softmax normalization to produce attention weights that determine contextual influence.
